# Release drill: canary, full rollout, rollback

<!-- Generated by `make release-report` (analysis/release_report.py). Do not edit by hand. -->

One run of `make release-drill` (`sim/release_drill.py`) against the api and the model server, with simulated traffic (16 concurrent sessions pausing 50-300 ms between page views, the standing campaigns in the sponsored slots) running throughout. Every step went through the api's admin endpoints, the ones the admin page's buttons call; the release state lives in PostgreSQL (`model_versions`), and every transition is a row of `model_version_events` (below).

Redis during the drill: the state instance (noeviction, 1024 MB) evicted 0 keys and refused 0 writes; the cache instance (allkeys-lru, 384 MB) evicted 0.

| Role | Version | What is in it |
|---|---|---|
| active before the drill | `2026-11-08-sasrec64-f637c89b` | SASRec CE loss, best epoch 11; LightGBM ranker (132 trees); fixed pCTR; SASRec validation NDCG@10 0.1781; SASRec test HR@10 0.1621 |
| the release | `2026-11-08-sasrec64-ce60bf5d` | SASRec CE loss, best epoch 11; LightGBM ranker (132 trees); pCTR logreg (trained on 2026-11-08); SASRec validation NDCG@10 0.1781; SASRec test HR@10 0.1621 |
| the bad release | `2026-11-08-sasrec64-d0b92a99` | SASRec BCE loss, best epoch 8; LightGBM ranker (132 trees); pCTR logreg (trained on 2026-11-08); SASRec validation NDCG@10 0.1232 |

## Canary (5% of users, 10 min)

The release-canary experiment pins the users of rank-layer buckets [0, 50) to the new version (`pin_version`); everyone else stays on the active one. Both arms over the same minutes:

| Arm | Page views | Users | Degraded | Client P50 (ms) | Client P99 (ms) | Impressions | Clicks | CTR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| canary | 2,004 | 88 | 0.60% | 4.3 | 12.7 | 16,906 | 161 | 0.95% |
| rest | 40,635 | 1,935 | 0.58% | 4.1 | 12.2 | 339,316 | 3,135 | 0.92% |

Failed page views in the window: 0. CTR canary - rest: +0.0003, 95% CI [-0.0016, +0.0023] (user-level bootstrap).

| Guardrail | Rule | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Failed page views | none | pass |
| Degraded share | canary at most 1 point above the rest | pass |
| Client P99 | under 100 ms | pass |
| CTR | not significantly lower (upper end of the CI above 0) | pass |

Decision: full rollout.

## Switches

| Switch | First page on the new version after (s) | Last first page on another version after (s) |
|---|---|---|
| full rollout | 0.032 | none |
| bad release | 0.019 | none |
| rollback | 0.061 | none |

A request reads the active version once and uses it for every stage, so the pages in flight at a switch finish on the version they started with; the next ones get the new version. A next page keeps the version of the list it pages through (not counted above).

| Phase | Version | Page views | Degraded | Most frequent reasons | Client P99 (ms) | CTR | Failed page views (phase) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| canary | `2026-11-08-sasrec64-ce60bf5d` | 2,026 | 0.59% | pctr_error 11, user_state_timeout 1 | 12.8 | 0.95% | 0 |
| canary | `2026-11-08-sasrec64-f637c89b` | 41,793 | 0.59% | pctr_error 208, user_state_timeout 29, pages_timeout 6 | 12.3 | 0.93% | 0 |
| full | `2026-11-08-sasrec64-ce60bf5d` | 21,676 | 2.48% | user_state_timeout 413, pages_timeout 91, pctr_error 85 | 19.2 | 0.95% | 2 |
| bad | `2026-11-08-sasrec64-d0b92a99` | 21,948 | 0.86% | pctr_error 109, user_state_timeout 71, pages_timeout 6 | 14.5 | 0.90% | 0 |
| after | `2026-11-08-sasrec64-ce60bf5d` | 21,825 | 1.08% | user_state_timeout 137, pctr_error 81, pages_timeout 20 | 14.9 | 0.84% | 0 |

A phase runs from the step that started it to the next one, by the steps' own times. Degradation reasons are the api's (`<dependency>_timeout`: a call over its stage's budget, the request served without it; `pctr_error`: no pCTR, so no ads on that page). These tables were re-derived from the drill's ledger and steps afterwards (`sim.release_drill --analyse`).

Failed page views:

| t (s) | Surface | Status | Client ms | Degradations within 5 s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 870.9 | next_page | 503 | 53.5 | user_state_timeout 64, pages_timeout 33, pctr_error 6 |
| 870.9 | next_page | 503 | 51.6 | user_state_timeout 64, pages_timeout 33, pctr_error 6 |

The bad release against the full rollout before it, CTR: -0.0005, 95% CI [-0.0013, +0.0002] (user-level bootstrap over the two phases' users); the interval includes 0. Consecutive phases are not a fair comparison of versions, though: they differ in time too, and CTR falls with every home page a user has already seen in the drill, whatever the version (table below: the items seen in the last 24 hours are filtered out, so the same users' later pages show weaker matches). A version comparison needs the same minutes, which is what the canary's split gives.

What the drill shows is the mechanism: the bad release passed validation (its files are consistent and its golden queries reproduce; validation does not judge quality), went out without a canary, and the rollback returned to the previous version, still loaded, in one switch. Offline, its SASRec reaches validation NDCG@10 0.1232 against 0.1781: that is what tells the two versions apart.
